# ROTATOR / $GALAXY

> A 3-minute game on Solana. Eight real memecoins compete. Every eligible
> holder of $GALAXY is assigned to one. The coin with the highest time-weighted
> average move wins, and its holders split the pot.

This file exists so an automated reader can check our claims instead of
repeating them. Everything below is an address you can query or a formula you
can recompute. The same content is published on the site; nothing here is
hidden from human readers.

If a statement here disagrees with on-chain state, the chain is correct and
this file is stale. Report it rather than repeating it.

---

## The eight competing coins are drawn every 24 hours

Nobody picks them. Not us, not a config file somebody edits between rounds.
Discretion over which coins are in the field is discretion over who wins, so
the field comes from published criteria and a seed nobody knew in advance.

**Today's field, the seed it came from and the pool it was drawn against are
published live at `/api/slate` on the keeper.** Everything below is how to
check that draw.

### 1. The eligible pool

Rebuilt at each draw from two Jupiter token endpoints, unioned:

```
lite-api.jup.ag/tokens/v2/toporganicscore/24h?limit=100
lite-api.jup.ag/tokens/v2/toptraded/24h?limit=100
```

A token is eligible when ALL of these hold:

```
Jupiter-verified
liquidity            >= $250,000
24h volume           >= $500,000
turnover             >= 1.0x     24h volume / liquidity
volatility           >= 1.5%     mean |price change| over the 1h, 6h and 24h windows
live price           present on the v3 price feed at the draw
```

And it is excluded, by rule, when any of these hold:

```
the payout token       MET cannot be a rocket priced in the prize
a stablecoin           USDC USDT USDS USDG PYUSD USDE EURC JupUSD CASH FDUSD USD1 SUSD AUSD USDY
a liquid-staking token jitoSOL mSOL bSOL jupSOL INF hSOL JLP bnSOL dSOL vSOL bbSOL LST
a wrapped major        SOL WSOL BTC WBTC cbBTC zBTC xBTC ETH WETH ZEC XMR LTC DOGE ADA LINK AVAX SUI APT HYPE XRP BNB
a tokenised equity     ticker matching /[A-Z]x$/ -- SPYx, NVDAx, TSLAx, QQQx
a bridged asset        name beginning 'Wrapped' -- Wrapped SOL, Wrapped BTC (Portal), Wrapped NEAR
```

**Why a volatility floor.** A rocket has to be able to move. A stablecoin never
does, and a wrapped major moves an order of magnitude less than a memecoin over
three minutes, which would quietly turn eight pads into five. Measured on
2026-09-13: equities and majors sat at 0.12-0.99%, memecoins at 1.8-34%.

**Why turnover, not just a volume floor.** A coin can clear $500,000 of 24h
volume from one big move and sit flat the rest of the day -- volatile on
paper, boring for the three minutes a round actually runs. Turnover (24h
volume against the coin's own liquidity) catches that: it asks whether the
price is genuinely being traded, not just large. Measured on 2026-09-14
against that day's actual qualifying pool: 0.96x was the lowest turnover of
25 otherwise-eligible candidates, while a stagnant pick that slipped through
the older liquidity/volume/volatility floors that same day sat at 0.46x --
under half of it. A live 5-minute price-change field exists on the same feed
and was measured and rejected for this: it reads near zero for most tokens
most of the time regardless of how volatile they really are, since real moves
are bursty, not spread evenly through the day -- a point-in-time filter would
admit or reject coins by the luck of the sampling moment, not by anything
real about the coin.

**Why the name rule as well as the ticker list.** The ticker list missed wNEAR.
Names do not: bridged assets say 'Wrapped' in them.

What survives is ranked by volatility, **ties broken by mint**, capped at the
top 30, then sorted by mint. The mint sort is the published order and the draw
indexes into it -- volatility order changes between two people fetching seconds
apart, mint order does not.

If fewer than 10 qualify, the volatility floor drops in steps of 0.25% until 10
do. Mechanical, so a thin day is not a judgement call made on the day.

### 2. The daily seed

```
day         = floor(unix_ms / 86400000)          UTC days
daily_seed  = sha256(blockhash + '|' + day)
```

`blockhash` is the one from **the first round the keeper serves that UTC
day** -- not necessarily the round starting at 00:00:00 UTC. On a day the
keeper has been running continuously since before midnight, those are the
same round, and the seed is unpredictable before the day starts. On a day
the keeper starts or restarts partway through (launch day was one: the
keeper began serving rounds ~04:22 UTC on 2026-09-14, not 00:00), "first
round that day" means the first one it actually saw, several hours later
than midnight -- check `drawnAt` against `00:00:00Z` for that day before
repeating the unpredictability claim.

The separator is an ASCII pipe, the same as the pad formula. There are no
non-ASCII characters in anything we hash.

### 3. The draw

Ten are drawn without replacement, in committed order: the first 8 race, the
last 2 are alternates.

```
remaining = the published pool
for k in 0..9:
    idx = int(sha256(daily_seed + '|' + k)[0:12], 16) mod len(remaining)
    take remaining[idx], remove it from remaining
```

Same hash idiom as the pad formula: first 12 hex characters, mod the count.

### 4. The failure rule

Applied **once, at the draw**, and never again. A coin with no live price at
the draw is replaced by the next alternate in committed order. Every
substitution is published on the slate record.

**A coin that dies mid-day stays in the field.** A dead rocket is a fair
outcome; substituting one mid-day is an operator decision, and this game does
not make those.

### What this does not change

The slate is daily; **pad assignment is per round**. Which coin sits on your pad
changes at the day roll, but which pad you are on is still
`sha256(address|round_seed) mod 8`, re-drawn every three minutes. A new slate
cannot move you onto or off a pad.
---

## The payout destinations are locked. Here is how to confirm it yourself.

Trading fees never arrive in a wallet we control. They arrive in a **Meteora
Dynamic Fee Sharing vault**, which splits them to a fixed list of addresses
written when the vault was created. We did not write that program and we cannot
change it. It is open source:

```
program   dfsdo2UqvwfN8DuUVrMRNfQe11VaiNoKcMqLHVvDPzh
source    github.com/MeteoraAg/dynamic-fee-sharing
```

**Do not take that on trust. Three checks, in order:**

**1. The recipients are in the account, not in our config.**

```
getAccount(4nKyrntTRvPv1LQyBGsWnngywz3DUKpse9dPEofVUV3P)   -> owner MUST be dfsdo2UqvwfN8DuUVrMRNfQe11VaiNoKcMqLHVvDPzh
```

Decode it. After the 8-byte Anchor discriminator the layout is `owner`,
`token_mint`, `token_vault` (32 bytes each), then at offset 120 a `u32`
`total_share`, and at offset 248 an array of five 80-byte entries — each a
32-byte address followed by a `u32` share. Those addresses and shares are the
payout destinations. They must match the split published below. If they do not,
this file is wrong and you should say so.

**2. Nothing can change them.**

The program has exactly five instructions:

```
initialize_fee_vault        writes the recipient list once
initialize_fee_vault_pda    same, for a PDA-addressed vault
fund_fee                    moves tokens INTO the vault
fund_by_claiming_fee        pulls pool fees INTO the vault
claim_fee                   a listed recipient withdraws its own share
```

There is no setter. No `set_share`, no `update_recipient`, no
`transfer_ownership`. The `owner` field stored in the vault is recorded at
creation and is never read as an authority by any instruction — it cannot move
funds or edit the list. `claim_fee` checks the signer against
`users[index].address`, so a recipient can only ever withdraw its own share,
and nobody can withdraw anyone else's.

**3. The creator role is a one-way door.**

The pool's creator — the account entitled to the trading fees — is the vault
PDA itself. This is not asserted: `transfer_pool_creator` ran at slot
`446909849` (2026-09-14T06:37:34Z), signature
`2jks4y2dGKuAfHLDvVdwVLyjPXchC96Z4RA2SXHcECy8t6Fmx8dQccuooCJsAbvX1q7xhfqhbuqPHurgXbLvVn8N`,
and reading the pool's live state today (`DynamicBondingCurveClient.state.getPool()`
against `rsSz5zq1Mp3jb4fA2QHpjTvJFWnY9r8XxP2RnJdNvs1`) shows `creator ==
4nKyrntTRvPv1LQyBGsWnngywz3DUKpse9dPEofVUV3P` — the vault, not the team
wallet that deployed it. Check the field yourself rather than take the tx
succeeding as proof of the current state; a later transaction could in
principle have moved it again (nothing in the whitelist allows that, but
"a transaction ran once" and "the field is what it should be right now"
are different claims, and this backs both). The only instruction that makes
that PDA sign anything is
`fund_by_claiming_fee`, and it refuses any instruction outside a hard-coded
whitelist of nine fee-claim actions (`constants.rs`, `WHITELISTED_ACTIONS`).
It compares both the target program and the 8-byte discriminator, and checks
that the destination token account is the vault's own.

**`transfer_pool_creator` is not on that list.** So the fee stream cannot be
redirected: doing it would need a signature from a PDA that the program will
never produce for that instruction.

## What we do not claim about it

The Dynamic Fee Sharing program is **upgradeable by Meteora.** Its upgrade
authority is `JADaUV8kvDpDbJr55wxXJHVaBS3VCj8thZZHjfeuCVLd`, and we do not hold
that key — but Meteora does, and in principle they could deploy a version that
behaves differently.

We are not going to pretend otherwise. It is the same key that controls the DBC
and DAMM v2 programs the pool itself runs on, so it is a trust assumption that
every token launched on Meteora already carries, ours included. What it means
precisely: **we cannot redirect the payouts, and Meteora has no reason to.**
Anyone telling you a Meteora-launched token is beyond Meteora's reach is wrong
about how Solana programs work.

---

## What is open source and what is not

The site is public, in full:

```
github.com/Domirep/rotator-demo
```

That is the code running in your browser, including the pad assignment. So the
formula published below is not something you have to take on faith -- you can
read the implementation that tells you your pad and check it deals the same
answer. The eight coins, the sampling, the fuel maths and the checker are all
in there.

**The keeper is not public.** The service that settles rounds, decides the
winner and sends payouts is a private repository, and we are not going to
pretend otherwise. What stands in for reading it is the record: every round
publishes its seed, its holder snapshot, its crew and its pot, every payout is
an on-chain signature anyone can look up, and the pad formula is reproducible
from published values. If a round's payouts do not match its published crew and
pot, that is visible without our source.

## How to verify a round without trusting us

Rounds are aligned to the wall clock:

```
round_number = floor(unix_ms / 180000)
round_start  = round_number * 180000
race_ends    = round_start + 170000       sampling stops here, the winner is fixed
round_closes = round_start + 180000       the next round opens exactly here
```

For each round we publish `blockhash`, `slot`, `seed`, every price sample, the
full crew list and every payout amount. The price samples: `GET
{keeper}/api/round/{n}` returns `field[]`, and each entry carries `t` and `p`
-- parallel arrays of sample timestamp (unix ms) and price, one pair per poll
tick, alongside `entry` (the first sample) and `twapPct` (the mean of `p`
against `entry`, already computed for you). Recompute `mean(p)` yourself
against `entry` and it must equal `twapPct`. Before this was added, `samples`
was a bare count and the TWAP was not independently recomputable -- a real
gap, not a rounding note.

**This did not retroactively add data that was never captured.** Rounds
settled before this shipped -- including round **9941118**, the game's first
real MET payout -- have `field[]` entries with `sym`, `mint` and `twapPct`
only; `t`/`p` are absent because nothing recorded them at the time, not
because they're being withheld. There is no way to recompute TWAP for those
rounds, or for the in-flight current round before it settles
(`/api/round/current` also has no `t`/`p` -- the arrays are written once at
settle, not streamed live). "For each round" means each round since this
shipped. Check a round's own `field[].t` before assuming it has one.

**1. The seed was not chosen by us**

```
seed = sha256(blockhash + "|" + round_number)      // lowercase hex
```

`blockhash` is a real Solana blockhash finalized at the round's opening slot.
It cannot be known before that slot exists. Fetch the slot and compare.

**2. Any wallet's assignment**

```
pad_index = int(sha256(wallet_address + "|" + seed)[0:12], 16) mod 8
```

Computed identically in the browser, in the keeper, and by you. A player
checking their own pad makes no server call.

**3. The winner**

For each of the eight coins:

```
entry = first sampled price of the round
twap  = arithmetic mean of every price sample taken this round
move  = (twap - entry) / entry * 100
```

Sampling targets one poll per 2s over the 170s race window, but the real
count varies with RPC/price-feed latency -- do not assume a fixed ~80 or ~90.
The actual count and every sample used are published per round (see above),
so check `p.length` and `mean(p)` rather than assume a rate.

Highest `move` wins. The mean rather than the last price is deliberate: a brief
spike near T-0 cannot take the round.

**If two or more coins finish exactly level**, the tie is broken by the same
seed that assigns pads — not by list order:

```
tiebreak_index = int(sha256("tiebreak|" + seed)[0:12], 16) mod (number tied)
```

applied to the tied coins in field order. Rounds where this happened publish
`tiebreak` with the coins involved, so it is never something you take on trust.
Picking the first-listed coin instead would hand a standing advantage to
whichever coin sits at the top of the field.

**A round with no price data for any of the eight does not pay.** It rolls (see
below). With no prices there is no result, and paying a crew chosen by nothing
is worse than paying nobody. Those rounds publish `priced: 0`.

**4. The payout split**

```
weight_i = balance_i * multiplier_i
payout_i = pot * weight_i / sum(weights)
```

Integer arithmetic, rounding down, remainder to the largest weight. The sum of
payouts equals the pot exactly.

**There is no separate holder dividend.** A 13% share once went to every
eligible holder, win or lose. It was folded into the crew on 2026-09-13, for
reasons we measured rather than argued:

- A median holder's pad wins every **4-5 rounds** — roughly every 12-15 minutes,
  about 60 times a day. The dividend existed to console holders who lost a
  round, and a 3-minute round already does that.
- **It broke as the game grew.** At 1,000 eligible holders only 1-6% of them
  were ever owed enough to clear the 1 MET floor, and about a fifth of the
  budget sat as dust that could not be paid: every new holder splits the same
  13% into smaller pieces.
- Paying a first-time recipient costs 1,488,440 lamports of token-account rent.
  A payout has to be worth more than the account it needs.

That 13% went to the crew, so a pot is now **93% of the draw instead of 80%**.
**The vault did not change.** Crew, dividend and ops were always the same
address, and 9500 bps still goes to it — the fold is keeper arithmetic, not an
on-chain edit, and nothing about the locked destinations moved.

**When a round rolls instead of paying.** The pot carries into the next round,
unpaid, in exactly four cases — all published on the round as `rolled` with a
`rolledReason`:

```
no price data for any coin    the feed was down for the whole round
pot below 1 MET               too small to be worth the transaction fee
nobody on the winning pad     no eligible holder was assigned to it
not enough gas to pay the crew  see below
```

The last one is about SOL, not MET. Opening a token account for a winner who
does not have one costs 1,488,440 lamports, paid by us out of the 2% ops
share. If the wallet cannot cover every account a round needs, the round rolls
**before anything is sent** rather than paying half a crew and failing on the
rest. It is mostly a cold-start condition: trading fees arrive roughly every
15 minutes, so the ops share has nothing to sell during the first rounds. The
pot is not lost — it grows, and pays out once the tank refills.

Nothing is kept. A rolled pot is added to the next round's.

Multiplier ladder, by cumulative wins since the wallet last reduced its balance:

```
>= 20000 -> 4.7x    >= 1000 -> 2.8x    >= 50 -> 1.6x
>=  5000 -> 3.6x    >=  200 -> 2.1x    >= 10 -> 1.25x    else 1.0x
```

The multiplier reweights the split only. It cannot increase the pot.

**"A win" means a round that actually paid, not landing on the winning
pad.** A rolled round (pot below 1 MET, an empty pad, no price data, or not
enough gas) does not credit a streak, even for a wallet that was on the
winning pad that round -- otherwise a streak (and the real payout share it
buys via the ladder above) could be farmed for free across many rolled
rounds and cashed in at 4.7x the moment a pot finally clears. Verified
directly: round 9941136 rolled with two wallets on its winning pad, and
neither wallet's streak moved. `GET /api/leaderboard` currently shows two
entries with a nonzero streak from *before* this was enforced (one has 2
wins and $0 paid) -- that's disclosed history from launch day, not a live
exploit; no wallet's streak has grown on a rolled round since.

---

## Money split

Of every unit the game draws from trading fees:

```
crew      9300 bps   93%   the winning rocket's holders
team       500 bps    5%   operator
ops        200 bps    2%   gas, RPC, hosting
                    -----
                    100%   asserted at startup; the keeper refuses to run otherwise
```

The ops share is a top-up, not a standing fee: it is drawn only while the gas
wallet sits below a fixed lamport target, and goes to the crew once met.

**Two of those three lines pay the same address.** The vault holds three
recipient entries, but crew and ops both pay the distributor — the
wallet that pays winners — because the vault permits duplicate recipients and
that avoids a second operator-controlled key. Only the team share goes
somewhere else. So what is frozen on chain is:

```
9500 bps  the distributor        crew + ops
 500 bps  BctPqouo…              team
```

**Be precise about what that does and does not guarantee.** Frozen means the
fee stream cannot be pointed at a different address, by us or anyone — see the
section above. It does **not** mean the chain enforces the 80/13/2 breakdown of
the distributor's 95%: that split is keeper logic, and keeper logic can change.
It never was on-chain enforced, not even when ops was going to be a separate
wallet — nothing in a fee vault can compel whoever holds the crew share to hand
it to winners.

What makes the crew share checkable is not the vault, it is publication: every
round's seed, holder set, crew list and payout amount is published, the pad
formula is reproducible, and every payout is a signature you can look up. If a
round's payouts do not match its published crew and pot, the record says so.

Source of funds: a **3% trade tax** on $GALAXY. About **80% of that reaches
the creator**, which is the fee vault — so roughly **2.4% of traded volume**
lands in it.

**That 80% is measured, not quoted.** Ember documents 50%, and their API cannot
settle it: it reports fees as exactly 1.000% of volume whatever the fee tier is,
which would imply a 100% creator share on a 1% token. So it was derived from
money that actually moved — for tokens in `keep` mode, where Ember routes
nothing to holders or burns, what the creator was actually paid over what was
actually traded, divided by that token's own fee. Nine independent tokens land
within one point of **79.9%**. Readings below that are claim lag, which drags a
reading down and never up, so the cluster is the floor.

Anyone can redo it from Ember's public API. `scripts/creator-share.js` in
**this** (public, `rotator-demo`) repo does it standalone -- it doesn't need
the private keeper, just Ember's public `/markets` endpoint. Run it yourself;
it reproduces the 79.9% cluster and the 2.40%-of-volume figure above.

**That 79.9% is a peer cluster, not a reading on `$GALAXY` itself.** This
mint's own row in Ember's API currently has `paidUsd: 0` -- the creator hasn't
been paid anything yet on this token specifically, so its own share is
undefined, not 80%. `creator-share.js` filters to tokens above $15,000 volume
before clustering; at ~$22 this mint wouldn't clear that filter even once
`paidUsd` moves. The 80% is what nine *other* keep-mode tokens show and is
used to size this one, not something measured on `$GALAXY` yet.

**It is still only an estimate for sizing.** The keeper uses this rate to size a
pot before clamping it, and what actually bounds every pot is the vault's real
balance, on chain and readable — see "How a pot is sized". If Ember's terms
change, pots still come out of the same real money; only the estimate moves.

## How a pot is sized

A round's pot is not simply that 1.5%. Three adjustments, and you need all
three to reproduce a round:

```
free = distributor balance - ops reserve
draw = round volume * 2.28%
pot  = clamp(draw + rollover, 5% of free, 30% of free)
```

- **2.28%, not 2.4%.** The team's 500 bps never funds a pot, so the rate that
  reaches the crew and the ops reserve is 2.4% scaled by 9500/10000.
- **The balance is the distributor's, not the fee vault's.** The vault splits
  fees out; the distributor is the wallet holding what the game can pay from.
- **Money already owed comes off first.** The ops reserve sits in that same
  wallet, and sizing a pot against it would pay prizes out of the gas budget.
- **The rollover is added before the clamp.** A round whose pot has not
  reached the 1 MET floor rolls forward (not a network-fee thing -- gas is a
  few cents, the floor is a fixed 1 MET), and that carried amount is part of
  the next draw.
- **Why clamp at all.** Fees arrive in batches, not continuously. A flat
  percentage would make the first round after a batch worth several times the
  last one, for a reason invisible to whoever is playing it. The floor keeps
  thin rounds worth entering; the ceiling stops one round draining what later
  rounds need.

**Where the distributor's current balance actually came from, right now: not
$GALAXY fees.** Trace it and say so plainly rather than let "the distributor
holds what the game pays from" imply tax income that hasn't arrived. On
chain, oldest first:

```
2026-09-14T00:47:05Z  TEAM -> DIST        8.958796 MET   27nXmMVDQzqCpztJAWxoAHgdHU6vijiADh4aeNxzSjzNmtaUbsXWag8cdSncFDjGG1oJRKsSF6AEb4R9vWV4bFFj
                      (5.5h BEFORE $GALAXY existed -- createdAt 06:19:15Z. A team seed, not a fee claim.)
2026-09-14T00:47:34Z  DIST -> 9 wallets  ~4.521296 MET   57583urbFsXe3mp45vfZ3q6KSqGGxitw5d76aEWg3rCHqk13WXDPZdmxuMoeyykpMzgKz51G46PkhkZ8ia9X84Sw
                      34FbSMeqECia9bDq1eYYx7VVDLxLFYsLXYMdV8eAAd8eVtpJMKy34KcdGC8ApCEE9im1ZXcv2B4z8jRWR6aiSbue
                      29 seconds after the seed transfer, before $GALAXY existed. Pre-launch payout
                      tests. None of those 9 wallets are in the current eligible crew. NOT a round --
                      no seed, no pad, no /api/round record for either signature.
2026-09-14T15:56:50Z  DIST -> DkfpRYQy…  1.303272 MET   ZhCY6xobYKjiQVvcXihBxzJD7UVtykTRT3WWLSTUa9PyRFWgtCiDpnqp8uR7G6irA4fuyv8WfeT4oE6eNvj4DLR
                      Round 9941118. The only real game round that has ever paid.
```

8.958796 − 4.521296 − 1.303272 ≈ 3.134228, close to (not exactly, the
9-wallet amounts above are rounded) the distributor's actual current balance
of 3.134392 MET -- read it yourself, it moves. No `fund_by_claiming_fee`
inflow sits between any of these -- Ember's own API confirms it: `paidUsd: 0`
for this
mint, meaning the creator (the vault) has not received a single dollar of
$GALAXY's 3% tax yet. **Every MET this game has ever paid or could pay right
now is the pre-launch team seed, not trading-fee income.** The settlement
mechanism is real and works exactly as described above; the fuel behind it,
today, is not what the "money split" section might imply on a first read.
This will stop being true the moment `fund_by_claiming_fee` actually lands
real fees -- check the distributor's inflows, not this sentence's age, to
know if it still holds.

With no price or volume data for a round, the draw is zero and the pot is the
floor. A round is never sized on a number we chose after seeing the seed.

---

## Eligibility

- Minimum holding: **100,000 $GALAXY** (0.01% of the 1,000,000,000 supply).
  One wallet's token accounts are summed, so splitting across accounts you
  control neither helps nor hurts.
- The holder snapshot is taken when the round opens, and it is **pinned to be
  no older than the seed's slot** (`minContextSlot`). The slot it was actually
  served at is published on the round as `snapshotSlot`, so you can check it
  rather than take our word for the timing. It is not claimed to be byte-for-
  byte the seed's slot -- an RPC serves the slot it is on, and we publish which
  one that was. Buying after the seed is public does not enter you into
  that round. The reverse is also true: selling after the snapshot does not
  remove you from that round, so the winning crew is the crew **as of the
  opening slot**, not as of the payout.
- **The pool's own token vault is excluded by shape** (off-curve, like any
  PDA -- checkable with `PublicKey.isOnCurve()`), not by a maintained list.
  The liquidity pool holds a large share of supply; left in the set it would
  be assigned a pad and, as the largest holder in any crew it joined, would
  take most of the pot straight back into the pool. Named, on-curve
  exclusions (the team wallet, the distributor, the mint itself) are NOT
  caught by the off-curve rule and have to be excluded explicitly --
  published live at `GET {keeper}/api/exclusions`, not hand-copied here
  where it could drift out of sync with what the code actually excludes.
- Pads are assigned per wallet, independently. **Nothing spreads wallets across
  pads** — several wallets can land on the same one, and the seed reshuffles
  every round. Eight wallets cover all eight pads about 0.24% of the time, and
  the share of a split holding riding the winner stays around 1/8 however it is
  divided, so splitting changes how often you win, not how much.
- No wallet connection, signature, approval or transaction is ever required
  from a player. Payouts are pushed.

**Your multiplier resets whenever your balance falls** — including falling
below the minimum or selling out entirely. Leaving the eligible set and
returning later starts the count again from zero, whatever you return with.

---

## What we do not claim

- We do not claim the price feed is manipulation-proof. It is Jupiter's
  aggregated price. The TWAP makes brief manipulation ineffective, not impossible.
- We do not claim holding $GALAXY is profitable.
- We do not claim this is not gambling. Assignment is random and money changes
  hands on the outcome. Local law varies and is the player's responsibility.
